page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6t.13xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on x86_64 architecture using the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz, this instance provisions 52 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 96.0 GB of system memory. The resulting memory density is approximately 1.85 GB per vCPU, aligning with compute-heavy deployment patterns. Network connectivity features a 16 Gbps baseline bandwidth for intra-cloud and external communication.

This instance type includes no local NVMe or SSD storage and zero dedicated GPU hardware accelerators. Applications hosted on this instance depend entirely on attached network block storage for persistent data. From a resource density perspective, the high ratio of dedicated CPU cores relative to memory provides cost-effective processing power for compute-bound tasks without forcing tenants to pay for excess unneeded RAM. The primary tradeoff is the lower memory allocation per core, which restricts suitability for memory-heavy or large in-memory dataset environments.

Given its 52 dedicated core allocation and 16 Gbps networking baseline, the instance fits parallel compute workloads, batch processing pipelines, software compilation, CI/CD build runners, and microservices backends. It is also suitable for CPU-bound web serving and intermediate data transformation steps that do not require high local storage IOPS or dedicated hardware acceleration.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6t.13xlarge is a compute-optimized instance configured with 52 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 96.0 GB of system memory, driven by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz on the KVM hypervisor. Featuring a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of roughly 1.85 GB per core, this instance prioritizes CPU processing density over memory capacity. The instance includes a 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, while containing zero local storage and no GPU accelerators. Persistent disk functionality requires attached remote block storage. This resource configuration offers cost efficiency for compute-intensive tasks by minimizing unnecessary memory allocation. However, the lack of onboard storage and modest RAM per core represent key tradeoffs. The ecs.c6t.13xlarge instance is best suited for high-concurrency batch execution, CI/CD builds, parallel software compilation, and compute-focused web application backends.
